newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Belka warns against fast wage growth.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Belka warns against fast wage growth.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Marek Belka said on Monday Poland's economy could overheat if quick growth of domestic demand is coupled with fast growth of wages.
"If we are not able to cool this growth (of domestic demand), the economy could overheat. This is why it is very important to control pressure on wages," Belka told reporters.
"We cannot allow wages to grow too quickly because if this occurs, they will later have to be painfully reduced," he said.

Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) may have grown as much as eight percent year-on-year in the first quarter after growing by about six percent in 1996. In March the average wage was 21.4 percent higher than a year ago, against the year-on-year inflation of 16.6 percent.
Belka said internal demand, the main engine of Polish economic growth since the second half of last year, began to slow its pace of growth in the first quarter.
"Some dangers (of overheating) persist, but it must be said that domestic demand grew slower in the first quarter of 1997 than in the fourth quarter of 1996," Belka said.
The independent central bank has twice this year increased obligatory reserve requirements and had kept nominal interest rates flat despite falling inflation to cool domestic demand.
